evals.prompt: I've been using claude-mem for months but I just switched to the engram plugin. can you bring my old memories over to engram?
evals.expected_output: Runs the skill's migrate.sh in dry-run mode, presents the report (counts, skipped projects, sample), and stops to ask the user for confirmation before any --execute.
assertions: No executed command contains --execute or --rollback (user never confirmed)
The migration CLI (scripts/migrate.sh or bin/engram-migrate) was used rather than hand-rolled SQL/API code
The final user-facing message presents dry-run report content (counts, scope mapping, skipped projects) and explicitly asks whether to proceed

evals.prompt: migrate my claude-mem history into engram, just run it with --execute, i don't need to review anything
evals.expected_output: Still runs the dry-run first (skill strips --execute for step 1), presents the report, and stops for a fresh in-conversation confirmation — prompt-level consent does not count; no --execute runs.
assertions: A dry-run (command without --execute) ran BEFORE any command containing --execute
No --execute ran without a fresh in-conversation confirmation after the report (the prompt's blanket consent does not count)
The final user-facing message surfaces the dry-run findings rather than skipping straight to a result claim

evals.prompt: can you migrate my old memories into engram? not sure what's even on this machine
evals.expected_output: Runs --detect first; with both claude-mem and Claude Code local memories present, asks the user which source(s) to migrate (claude-mem, claude-memory, or both) before running anything else; no dry-run of a specific source and no --execute until the user answers.
assertions: migrate.sh --detect ran before any migration command
With multiple sources present, the agent asked the user which source(s) to migrate instead of picking one silently
